newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Illiquidity stifles Slovak bourse, SAX edges up.
newsitem.headline: Illiquidity stifles Slovak bourse, SAX edges up.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) opened the week with a quiet session on Monday, as a single bloc deal in steel maker VSZ pushed the SAX index 0.66 points higher to 194.21.
Trading on the BSE floor was dominated by a bloc deal in steel maker VSZ, of 25,187 shares traded at 710 crowns, up 10 from Friday.
Apart from this, only insignificant volumes were traded, devaluing any movements of the index, dealers said.
"It's unreasonable to watch the SAX seriously at the presence, as it is not backed by traded volumes," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.

He said the bourse remained paralyzed by instability on the money and forex markets, and by the turbulent political situation following a thwarted referendum last month, which was seen as a failed test of the country's commitment to democracy.
"We have unstable financial markets, an uncertain capital market and a poisoned political situation here at the moment," he said.
"Worst of all, none of these is showing even a sign of any further direction, which would help investors to orient themselves," Krutil added.
The most-capitalised Slovak share, oil refinery Slovnaft, closed down 19 crowns at 1,020 crowns, but traded only 42 shares on the bourse floor.
Overall volume eased to 409,938 shares, from 738,349 shares traded on Friday, while turnover fell to 128.71 million crowns, from 828.81 million.
